name: pdremove
description:
A ProDOS VOLUME MOUNTED WITH -o write LOSES FILES AND DIRECTORIES AS ProDOS 8 LOSES THEM, AND THE BLOCKS COME BACK.  /dev/sd1 is a fresh disk/pdscratch.po; /testdata/pdremove removes through pdmount -r/-J/-D/-O and the check script reads the volume the machine left.

ON THE SCREEN:
  mw=0      mount -o write mounted writable.
  PDRM ._ext errno=1   a resource fork does not go on its own: EPERM.
  PDRM sap errno=1 / f02 errno=1   a clear destroy bit ($80) refuses: EPERM.
  PDRM nosuch errno=2  a name that is not there.
  PDRM hello errno=13  uid 1 cannot take a name from a 755 root-owned directory.
  PDRM hello/tree/ext/f01 errno=0   a seedling, a tree, a GS/OS extended file and a seedling go.
  PDRD sub/inner errno=66   a directory with a file in it: ENOTEMPTY.
  PDRD sub/inner/deep errno=20   rmdir of a file: ENOTDIR.
  PDRM sub/inner/deep errno=0, PDRM sub errno=1   the file goes; unlink of a directory is EPERM.
  PDRD sub/inner errno=0   the emptied directory goes.
  PDOU f03 5000 gone=2 bad=0   a file unlinked while open: its name is gone, and 5000 bytes written through the descriptor read back.
  PDCR big / PDWR big 20000   a new file takes the freed blocks.
  um=0      the unmount, after the unlinked file's last close gave its blocks back.

IN THE CHECK SCRIPT (pdremove_check.py): cadius CHECKVOLUME silent (after a control it must flag) -- so every freed block is free and no live block is; the removed entries are gone and every directory's file count, links and pointers hold; every file left is byte-identical in cadius's extraction; big's blocks all belonged to removed files; and each removed index block that was not reused is written back flipped, as ProDOS 8 and GS/OS leave one.
